answers.answer: Chi is a composable Go HTTP routing library for services and REST APIs. Application authors construct routers, register handlers/middleware, and pass the router to net/http; the HTTP server invokes its handler interface. The repository also exercises it from Go tests and example applications. This is library usage, not a standalone chi server daemon.

The root chi package contains public router interfaces/constructor (chi.go), Mux registration/dispatch (mux.go), radix-tree endpoint matching (tree.go), request routing state and parameter access (context.go), and middleware composition (chain.go). middleware/ supplies optional net/http wrappers. _examples/ contains consuming applications; *_test.go supplies tests/benchmarks. render and docgen are external companion modules, not root routing implementation.

Go source, Go modules, and standard net/http/context organize the library; root go.mod declares github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 and go 1.24 without third-party requirements. Root package chi and subpackage middleware are distinct Go package boundaries. _examples/rest and _examples/versions have separate Go 1.16 modules: rest-example requires chi/docgen/render; versions requires chi/render plus indirect ajg/form. Tests use Go testing and httptest. I did not verify a CI build command.

Public setup starts at chi.NewRouter (chi.go:62), returning NewMux. Register routes, optionally Use middleware, then supply the router to http.ListenAndServe. HTTP execution enters Mux.ServeHTTP (mux.go:63), which prepares/reuses routing context and invokes its composed handler.

Mux.routeHTTP (mux.go:455-499) orchestrates method/path dispatch. node.FindRoute (tree.go:383-406) delegates radix traversal to node.findRoute (410-557), returning the method-specific endpoint handler.

Direct source dependencies: RouteCtxKey/*Context (context lookup); methodMap (index lookup); mx.tree.FindRoute (call); Context.RoutePattern (call); Mux.MethodNotAllowedHandler and NotFoundHandler (calls). The returned h.ServeHTTP is dynamic interface dispatch; Request.SetPathValue is external net/http. Direction is established by expressions inside routeHTTP, not inferred reverse links. Lattice returned zero incoming/outgoing call edges even with includeEstimated=true; that is incomplete graph evidence, not proof of no calls.

TestMuxPlain constructs NewRouter and registers GET /hi with a closure writing bye. Registration: Get -> handle -> InsertRoute -> setEndpoint stores that callback under mGET. Test transport: httptest.NewServer(r), then testRequest builds GET ts.URL+/hi and calls http.DefaultClient.Do. Server -> Mux.ServeHTTP -> composed handler -> routeHTTP -> FindRoute -> findRoute -> stored handler's ServeHTTP -> closure -> ResponseWriter.Write. With no middleware, chain returns its endpoint. testRequest reads the response body; the test expects bye. HTTP transport/server invocation, interface dispatch, callback selection and response writing are dynamic boundaries; this is source-supported flow, not an observed run.
The direct production Mux consumers are Find and routeHTTP, each calling mx.tree.FindRoute. Match is indirect through Find, not a third direct caller.

TestMuxPlain exercises dispatch end-to-end: GET /hi must yield bye, while GET /nothing-here must yield its custom not-found body. It enters through httptest.NewServer(r) and testRequest/http.DefaultClient.Do, reaching Mux.ServeHTTP and then routeHTTP. The test is source evidence; no tests were executed in this trial.

routeHTTP chooses Context.RoutePath, otherwise URL.RawPath then URL.Path, defaulting empty to /. FindRoute resets current-match state; findRoute consumes static prefixes, captures parameter/regexp/catch-all segments, validates constraints, and backtracks captured values on failure. Endpoint paramKeys originate from registered patterns. Successful keys/values append to Context.URLParams, preserving the subrouter stack. chi.URLParam -> URLParamFromCtx -> Context.URLParam searches newest keys first. routeHTTP exports captures through Request.SetPathValue and assigns Request.Pattern. Mount shifts RoutePath via nextRoutePath and clears its connecting wildcard value. Optional CleanPath middleware applies path.Clean; core matching itself does not universally clean/decode paths.
